text:
Maya Chen: Heads up — planning to bring the demo box for the Lisbon offsite (it's basically 2 laptops, external SSD, and a small battery pack). Anyone shipped demo gear vs carrying it through EU customs? Tips?

Samir Patel: I shipped once via DHL for Berlin summit. Pro: no lugging. Con: tracking anxiety and needed a customs invoice. Arrived 2 days late :grimacing:

Jules: I always carry the battery bank and SSD in carry-on, shipped the bigger metal case. Airline staff were meh about the case as checked. Remember: label batteries in carry-on and tape terminals.

Lina Torres: If you declare electronics to customs, keep receipts and serials handy. For EU I just showed purchase emails on my phone — quick.

OpsBot: Quick checklist reminder:
- batteries >100Wh: airline approval required
- spare li-ion: carry-on only
- have invoice/customs form if shipping

Samir Patel: Mini checklist I used (saved me):
```
Packing checklist:
- laptop x2 (serials saved)
- external SSD (in carry-on)
- battery packs <100Wh (carry-on)
- printed invoice & a PDF on phone
- low-value shipping label (declared for demo use)
```

Maya Chen: Sweet — do people prefer ship-to-hotel or ship-to-conference venue?

Jules: Ship-to-hotel worked for me once, front desk held it. Conference venue was easier but required a contact person. Ask the venue for receiving instructions.

Lina Torres: Pro tip: if you must carry GPUs/PC components, bring the manufacturer boxes and pics of ownership — customs sometimes flags high-value electronics.

Maya Chen: Thanks all. I'll split — carry SSDs and batteries, ship the case to the hotel with a stub contact. Anything else I missed?

Samir Patel: Take photos of everything before you leave, and a screenshot of airline battery rules (they change). :thumbsup:

Jules: Also pack a few zip ties and a slim toolkit — saved me when a screw came loose mid-demo.

Maya Chen: Awesome. Filing this away for the travel doc. :sparkles:
